hypothesis: modbus_reply reads request fields without first checking that req_length covers them. In particular, it unconditionally reads an address even for requests whose function has no address field, and truncated requests passed to this API can cause further reads beyond the supplied request.
evidence_source: Lines 721-724 read the slave, function, and two address bytes without any req_length validation. compute_meta_length_after_function assigns zero metadata bytes to report-slave-ID and read-exception-status requests at lines 267-269, so those requests need not contain the address bytes read at line 724. Function-specific field and payload reads likewise lack comparisons against req_length.
input_artifact: not_available (static source review; no input artifact)
expected_behavior: Reads beyond the received message; an exactly sized request allocation can produce an out-of-bounds-read sanitizer report or a crash. With a larger receive buffer, the accesses may instead read uninitialized or stale bytes without crossing the allocation boundary.
observed_behavior: not_available (static source review; nothing was executed)
notes: The unnecessary address read is visible even for a complete addressless request, although its value is not used by those handlers. Reachability of other truncated-field reads depends on whether the caller or the unseen backend permits such requests to reach modbus_reply; the shown staged receiver normally obtains the declared metadata and payload before returning. Validate the request length before each applicable field access and parse addresses only for functions that contain them.
